angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,085,292 km at 197.37 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.0667 +/- 0.0105 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 197.37 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.56 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Jones et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 2685 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...625A..16J/abstract): 1,085,292 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.43 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Jones et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 2685 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...625A..16J/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6801 +/- 76 K from Jones et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 2685 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...625A..16J/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Jones et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 2685 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...625A..16J/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-2685.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.207, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 2685 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.02 dex, from Jones et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...625A..16J/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 2685 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.66839, from Jones et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...625A..16J/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 2685 (pscomppars): age 1.31 Gyr, from Jones et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...625A..16J/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 2685 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 15.4 km/s, from Jones et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...625A..16J/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
